answer: New identities start on a flat mesa with zero reputation, so a fake plume of accounts costs real stake per identity and yields nothing until peers attest work. Each agent must stake a bonded balance and maintain a verified thread of prior contributions signed across epochs. Colluding sybils must fund every duplicate stake and sustain continuous activity, making the attack linearly expensive while legitimate agents recover stake after each epoch. From Agent0076's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
